questions.q: What makes Meridian Trust Bank's 162 custom roles a real finding rather than just visual clutter?
options: It makes the platform slower to load
It defeats quarterly access reviews — a reviewer can't tell which of nine overlapping roles on one user is actually load-bearing
ServiceNow has a hard limit of 100 custom roles per instance
Custom roles are never allowed on a production instance
questions.explain: Role sprawl's real cost is that it makes access reviews unreadable, which quietly defeats the control meant to catch inappropriate access.

questions.q: In Finding 2, why is the inconsistency between the `ssn` ACL and the `annual_income` ACL a genuine design-pattern failure?
options: Because the `annual_income` field should not exist on the `customer` table at all
Because scripted ACLs always run before role-only ACLs
Because both fields are comparably sensitive, but one is gated by a purpose-built role in a script and the other by the generic `itil` role over a thousand employees already hold
Because ServiceNow does not support role-only field-level ACLs
questions.explain: The sensitivity of the data has no relationship to the strength of the control — a direct symptom of no consistent, table-wide field-level security pattern.

questions.q: Why is Meridian's ServiceNow instance still on local authentication a specific, nameable finding rather than a minor convenience?
options: It directly contradicts the bank's own enterprise SSO + MFA standard, leaving the instance holding privileged IT, security, and HR data on the weakest available authentication path
Local authentication is always faster for end users than SSO
ServiceNow does not support SAML-based SSO at all
Okta cannot be configured as an identity provider for ServiceNow
questions.explain: Local-vs-SSO isn't cosmetic — it's a real contradiction between the bank's own authentication standard and what the instance actually enforces.

questions.q: What does Finding 4 (no audit logging on `ssn` or `annual_income`) mean Meridian currently cannot do?
options: Meridian cannot store SSNs or annual income data at all
Meridian cannot apply any ACL to those fields until auditing is enabled
Meridian cannot produce a record of who read or changed those fields, even though an ACL may correctly limit who could
Meridian's dictionary entries for those fields do not exist
questions.explain: A correct ACL answers who could read a field; only the Audit flag and sys_audit answer who actually did. Without it, that second question has no answer.

questions.q: What is the defining discipline of a real security assessment, as this lesson frames it?
options: Counting the total number of ACLs on the instance
Rewriting every role on the instance before analyzing any of them
Interviewing only the original admin who built the instance four years ago
Listing specific, named findings, each tied to a concrete platform mechanism and the chapter concept it violates — not a vague "this seems insecure" impression
questions.explain: Citing the mechanism, not just the symptom, is what makes an assessment actionable for an engineering team.
